title: To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems
venue: SYSTOR '26 (19th ACM International Systems and Storage Conference), pages 52-65
paper_use: problem framing: disaggregated prefill/decode with a global KV pool
cost model: R(L) prefill recompute, T(B) fabric transfer, net benefit R - T
hardware calibration for LLaMA-3-8B on A100 and 25 GB/s fabric (alpha_bw=0.026 ms/token, alpha_flop=8e-6 ms/token^2, crossover 512 tokens)
workload taxonomy: text, image, video prefixes; drift, sessions, scan pollution
deviation: The paper's reference code evaluates R(L) as a piecewise envelope, max(alpha_bw*L, alpha_flop*L^2). The benchmark sums both terms as a conservative total-latency model and documents this in environment/data/COST_MODEL.md; the constants, cost objective, and workload taxonomy are unchanged.
independence: The benchmark ships its own simulator, trace generator, and baselines. No source code from the KVLearn repository is included, and the reference solution is an independent online decayed-LFU policy rather than the paper's learned PRP/CARS/ATC stack.
